name: clock-skew returns later unprocessed entries to ready and restamps every held and ready entry in commit order
the recovered clock starts from admittedHigh when it is above physNow
two skewed results in one response restamp twice, each in commit order
an acked entry keeps its stamps through a later recovery
a sent delete answered clock-skew in the same response follows its create's new born, so both land
a skewed create that a 409 returned to ready, then a delete of it: recovery moves the delete's born with the create's life, and both land
undo of a skewed held create folds the update of its record silently, so no born is left that recovery cannot move, and the independent edit lands
a notice is a snapshot: the recovery that moves the born an orphan carries leaves the notice as it was written
a clock-skew restamp gives every entry, another instance's included, a fresh tick of the recovering instance
clock-skew recovery restamps intents, never predictions: a later update keeps the server's born
a keyed put carrying its unchanged life keeps that stamp through a clock-skew restamp: the server's newer delete stands
